title: Vector Tables
body:
Table of [[Pointer]]s to [[ISRs]]

It lives at a fixed place in memory (address 0 upward on the [[Motorola 68000]]), and each
entry is a *vector*: the address of the handler for one interrupt or exception number. When
an interrupt is taken, the [[CPU]] uses the vector number as an index, loads the address it
finds there into the program counter, and jumps.

That indirection is the point. Installing your own handler is a matter of writing an
address into a table slot, no recompilation of anything else, which is how a program takes
over the [[VBL ISR|vertical blank]] and puts the old vector back on exit.

Same idea as a function-pointer table in C, and the same idea as a vtable for virtual
method dispatch. See [[Interrupts]] for where it sits in the sequence.
